name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.existsUnique_affineExtension
title: Mankiewicz extension on open connected domains

content.display_title: Mankiewicz extension on open connected domains
content.one_sentence_role: Glues local affine-isometry charts using their agreement on open overlaps.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces, $S\subseteq E$ a nonempty connected open set, and $T\subseteq F$ an open set. If $f:S\to T$ is a bijective isometry, there is a unique surjective real affine isometry $A:E\to F$ satisfying $A(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in S$.
content.assumptions: The source is open, connected and nonempty; the target is open; and the specified map is a distance-preserving bijection. No completeness or finite dimensionality is required. Target connectedness is not an independent hypothesis.
content.conclusion: Exactly one ambient affine isometry extends the entire given map $f$.
content.proof_summary: Produce charts from matching small balls. Their agreement near an overlap point forces global equality, making the chart assignment locally constant and therefore constant on the connected source.
proof_steps: At $x\in S$, openness gives positive radii $R_s,R_t$ with $B(x,R_s)\subseteq S$ and $B(f(x),R_t)\subseteq T$. Set $R=\min(R_s,R_t)>0$. Apply [Construction of a local affine-isometry chart](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L695-L786) with this same $f,x,R$ and the two smaller ball inclusions to obtain a surjective affine isometry $A_x$ agreeing with $f$ on $B(x,R/8)$.

The uniqueness mechanism is [Agreement on a nonempty open set determines the affine map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/OpenConnected.lean#L36-L71). If affine maps $A,B$ agree on a nonempty open set $u$, choose $c\in u$ and $\varepsilon>0$ with $B(c,\varepsilon)\subseteq u$. For $z\ne c$, set $a=\varepsilon/(2\|z-c\|)>0$ and $y=c+a(z-c)$. Then $\|y-c\|=\varepsilon/2$, so $c,y\in u$. Affinity gives $$0=A(y)-B(y)=a(A(z)-B(z)),$$ since $A(c)=B(c)$. Cancel $a$; at $z=c$ agreement is already known. Thus $A=B$ on the whole ambient space.

For each chosen chart $A_x$, let $r_x>0$ be a radius of agreement. If $y\in S$ and $\|y-x\|<r_x$, then $$u=(s\cap B(x,r_x))\cap B(y,r_y)$$ is open, contains $y$, and is a region on which both $A_x,A_y$ equal $f$. Step 2 gives $A_x=A_y$ globally. Thus $x\mapsto A_x$ is locally constant, exactly as required in [Gluing locally agreeing affine isometries](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/OpenConnected.lean#L74-L118).

Choose $x_0\in S$, using nonemptiness. On a connected space a locally constant map is constant: each fiber is open and its complement, a union of other open fibers, is open. Therefore $A_x=A_{x_0}$ for every $x\in S$. Put $A=A_{x_0}$; the local agreement at $x$ gives $A(x)=A_x(x)=f(x)$. If another affine isometry has this property, it agrees with $A$ on nonempty open $S$, so Step 2 proves uniqueness.
